memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: These are the decrees and laws you must be careful to follow in the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, has given you to possess—as long as you live in the land. Destroy completely all the places on the high mountains, on the hills and under every spreading tree, where the nations you are dispossessing worship their gods. Break down their altars, smash their sacred stones and burn their Asherah poles in the fire; cut down the idols of their gods and wipe out their names from those places. - Deut 12:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel prepared to enter the land, God's first instruction about worship was to tear down all the old places of idol worship — the altars, sacred stones, and poles scattered across the hills and under the trees. God wanted every trace of false worship removed, not merely reduced or relocated. Before true worship could fill the land, the false worship had to be cleared away completely. There was to be no blending of the old with the new, no keeping a few idols "just in case."

This decisiveness carries a lesson for our own hearts. When we come to God, He is not content to be added alongside our other loves and loyalties. The old idols must be torn down, not tucked away in a corner. We cannot serve God faithfully while quietly keeping altars to money, comfort, or self on the side. True worship requires clearing the ground of rivals.

This was a specific command to Israel about the physical idols of Canaan, and we are not called to literally destroy shrines today. But the principle endures. Paul writes that in Christ we are being made new, called to "put to death" whatever belongs to our old, sinful way of life (Col 3:5). The Spirit works in us to clear away the old idols so that Christ alone reigns. What false altars still stand in your heart? Ask God to help you tear them down completely, making room for wholehearted worship of Him alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "old altars" or idols am I keeping tucked away instead of tearing down?
- Do I try to add God alongside my other loyalties, or give Him first place alone?
- Where is the Spirit calling me to clear the ground for wholehearted worship?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You call me to tear down every idol and give You first place alone. Show me the false altars still standing in my heart, and by Your Spirit help me clear them completely, making room for wholehearted worship of You. Amen.
